result.title: Agent Money Benchmark: Can AI Agents Be Trusted to Spend Money?
result.summary: Giving an AI agent a wallet lets it buy data and services on a client's behalf. Trust then depends on how it spends money and what that spending achieves. We introduce Agent Money Benchmark (AMB) to test whether agents spend a client's money well, starting with purchases of information for financial decisions. We link seller quotes and payments to final answers, evaluating 12 models on 80 payment tasks with simulated sellers and 76 research questions using live data. Purchases settled in USDC on Solana mainnet via x402, a protocol for paying per web request. Three of the 12 models passed 79 of 80 payment tasks without payment or budget errors. Nine fell for a seller's trap at least once; repeat charges and above-list quotes accounted for 79% of scam events. We estimate waste from data and inference costs, counting failed payment tasks in full and research answers in proportion to missed points. With spending split equally between tracks, estimated waste ranged from \$21.0 per \$100 for Claude Fable 5.2 to \$70.8 for GPT-6 Luna.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Agent Money Benchmark，让 12 个模型在模拟卖家与真实链上支付环境下完成付款任务和信息购买型研究问题，统计支付错误、受骗事件，并把数据与推理开销折算为浪费金额来评估花钱是否值得。
AI.relevance_reason: 论文以货币成本衡量「付费获取信息」对最终答案的贡献，可能为 LVR 中证据获取的成本—收益权衡与停止决策提供外部评价思路，但完全不涉及视觉或 latent 状态，可供核查的迁移点较间接。
